title: Two ways to hold a mix
objectives: Compare separate funds for each asset class with a single hybrid or multi-asset fund.
State the SEBI rule for multi-asset allocation funds.
body_md:
Once the mix is set, there are two valid ways to hold it.

## Separate funds

One equity fund, one debt fund, one gold fund. More control over the mix, and the client sees each part clearly. The cost is that you have to rebalance it yourself.

## One all-in-one fund

Multi-asset, balanced advantage, aggressive or conservative hybrid funds hold several asset classes in one scheme. Simpler to run, and rebalancing inside the fund is not a taxable event for the investor.

## What SEBI requires

A multi-asset allocation fund must hold at least 10% in each of at least three asset classes. A balanced advantage fund changes its equity-debt mix dynamically, so always check the actual mix in the factsheet.

## How to choose

By the client's preference and portfolio size. A small portfolio is easier to run in one hybrid fund. A large one usually wants separate parts so the mix can be controlled. Both are valid; neither is automatically better.
example: A client with ₹8 lakh a year to invest chooses a multi-asset fund for simplicity, while a client with ₹80 lakh uses separate equity, debt and gold funds so the mix can be controlled precisely.
say: We can hold the mix in separate funds, or in one multi-asset fund if you prefer simplicity.
A multi-asset fund must hold at least 10% in each of at least three asset classes.
never: A hybrid fund is safer than equity.
The balanced advantage fund always holds 65% equity.

check.q: Under SEBI rules, a multi-asset allocation fund must hold…
o: At least 10% in each of at least three asset classes
check.why: That is the multi-asset mandate: at least 10% in each of at least three asset classes.

check.q: What is the main advantage of holding the mix in separate funds?
o: More control over the mix, though you have to rebalance it
check.why: Separate funds give control and visibility; the cost is that rebalancing is your job.

check.q: What should you check in a balanced advantage fund?
o: The actual equity-debt mix in the factsheet
check.why: A balanced advantage fund changes its mix dynamically, so the factsheet is the source.
